summary: The gate stamp holds up. The parser handles the three known gate shapes, and round 1's fixes (the two-gates refusal, the allow rule narrowed to `check`, the stricter `differs`) are in place; none of R1-1 to R1-10 needed raising again. The new findings sit at the edges: two README sentences that promise more than the code does, and the output cap from e5be593, which limits each check's streams but not the checker's whole result. IDs continue from R1-10, the numbers an earlier launch's round 1 already used on this PR; the guard refuses the reviewer the gate scripts, so these were traced by reading. Concurrency: this repository has no scheduled commands or queued jobs. Only a hand-run `stamp` writes checks.sh, and the precheck and the gate test only read it.

findings.title: Setup step 1 stamps before step 5 adds the parenthetical that stamp reads
findings.description:
Setup step 1 now ends "Then stamp it: <plugin>/scripts/redline-gate.sh stamp .claude/commands/agent-os/shape-spec.md .claude/redline/checks.sh", with no --steps. Without --steps, `stamp` takes its range from the "(gate steps M to N" parenthetical (scripts/redline-gate.sh lines 268-273, RANGE at line 66).

That parenthetical lives in the unattended section's point 7, which step 5 adds from templates/shape-spec-unattended.md (line 47). On a new repository, a person following the steps in order runs the command before that section exists. `stamp` then exits 2 with "has no \"(gate steps M to N\" parenthetical; give the command-step range with --steps <m>-<n>", the case tests/gate-test.sh line 175 pins. The template's TODO line (scripts/checks-template.sh line 34) gives the same command.

The message is clear, so this costs a retry, not a wrong stamp. Upgrading is unaffected: an existing repository already has the section.
findings.proposedFix: Move the stamping sentence from step 1 to after step 5, for example the end of step 5: "then stamp checks.sh: <plugin>/scripts/redline-gate.sh stamp ...". Or say in step 1 that, before step 5 exists, the range is given with --steps <m>-<n>. The unattended section sits outside the gate, so adding it never moves the hash, and step 7's `check .` holds either way.

findings.title: Gate stamp says any step added or removed moves the hash; a step with no backticks does not
findings.description:
The new Gate stamp paragraph says "any backticked change does, so a step added, removed, reordered or given a new flag moves the hash". That claims more than the code does.

Pass 3 of the parser (scripts/redline-gate.sh lines 148-178) puts only backticked spans and fenced lines into `hashed`. Step numbers and titles never enter it. So:
- A step written with no backticked span or fence, for example "9. **Lint** — run npm run lint and fix what it reports", can be added or removed without changing the hash.
- Two steps that swap places change it only when both hold spans.

The code, the script header (line 28, "Prose outside backticks never changes it") and the spec's decision (agent-os/specs/2026-10-21-1329-6-gate-stamp/shape.md, Decisions, "Prose edits never change it") all agree with each other. The README's "so" clause is what disagrees. The gate-test cases that add, remove and swap steps all use steps that hold spans (tests/gate-test.sh lines 152-160).
findings.proposedFix: Make the clause match the code and the decision: "any backticked change does, so a step that holds a backticked command moves the hash when it is added, removed, reordered or given a new flag. A step written wholly in prose does not, so a command step keeps its command in backticks." The README is outside the gate section of shape-spec.md, so nothing needs a restamp.

findings.title: The output cap is per check and per stream, so the checker's result is still unbounded
findings.description:
Commit e5be593 caps run_check's capture "so the checker's result fits the tool limit". Its message says the guard check alone was 30 KB and pushed the result into a file the checker may not read (agents/redline-checker.md line 5 disallows Read).

The cap does not bound the result. Each stream of each check is capped separately, and nothing caps the total:
- A failing check keeps up to 16384 bytes of stdout and another 16384 of stderr. One failing check with two long streams is already past the 30 KB that overflowed.
- Two failing checks reach about 32 KB of stdout alone, before the passing checks' 20-line tails, the git block and the stderr progress lines are added. Examples: `check` and `octane` after a broken service provider in a Laravel repository, or `guard` and `loop` here.

When the result overflows, the checker cannot return the JSON. `judge` (workflows/redline-loop.js lines 897-945) records a checker error, and `failingExcerpt` (lines 947-953) has no checks to excerpt. The round loses the failing output just when it is needed. The workflow itself reads at most the last 3000 characters of a failing check's stdout and 1500 of stderr (line 951).

.claude/redline/checks.sh lines 100-110 carry the same numbers. In this repository that file is a person's change (shape-spec.md point 11, agents/redline-shaper.md rule 7).

Question for the person: what should bound the checker's whole result?
findings.proposedFix:
Options for the person:
(a) Size each failing stream to what failingExcerpt reads, about 3 KB of stdout and 1.5 KB of stderr, and keep a passing check to about 1 KB. Six failing checks then stay under about 27 KB.
(b) Share one total budget, for example 16 KB, among the failing checks, so the bound holds however many fail.
(c) Keep the current caps and accept an overflow when more than one check fails.
(a) and (b) give the implementer less of a failing check in its own run, though it can Read an overflowed result, which the checker cannot. Whichever is chosen also needs a person to change the same lines in this repository's .claude/redline/checks.sh.

findings.title: `truncated` misses the byte cap, and the README contract still says 200 lines
findings.description:
`truncated` is true only when a stream has more lines than `keep`. A stream that is within the line count but over 16384 bytes is cut by `tail -c` and still reports `truncated: false`.

The README's output contract (README.md line 194, outside this diff) still shows `"stdout": "last 200 lines"` for every check and has no `truncated` field. Yet a passing check now keeps 20 lines, and both streams are capped at 16 KB.

Nothing reads `truncated` yet (no match in workflows/, agents/, skills/ or tests/), so this is about accuracy, not behaviour. .claude/redline/checks.sh lines 104-108 have the same lines, and changing them here is a person's change.
findings.proposedFix: Set `truncated` when either limit cut the stream: more lines than `keep`, or more bytes than `cap` (`wc -c` of the file against the cap). Update the README contract line to something like `"stdout": "the last 20 lines, 200 when the check failed, at most 16 KB"`, add `"truncated": false`, and add one bullet saying what `truncated` means. If R1-13 changes the caps, write the new numbers.
